gen-gf-tektur-gf-sofia-sans: Tektur has a pipe-cleaner look, thin and bendy and oddly oversized. Sofia Sans sits under it with rounded, tall letters and no stroke swelling, so the headline gets all the attitude.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-sono: Sono reads wide and friendly, its tall lowercase spaced out and each a left slightly ajar. Unica One is the opposite kind of voice, thin steel rod bent into commanding shapes, and it handles the shouting while Sono handles the talking.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-sofia-sans-semi-conde: Wallpoet cuts its letters with gaps like stencil lines. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed then carries a long page in a steady, unvarying line, with big entrances into every curve that keep the text easy to move through.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-stack-sans-headline: Expressive and loud, Warnes tapers its ink strokes out before they touch. Stack Sans Headline follows as a plain sans with a monoline skeleton and a deep middle band, grounding the showy top with something sturdy.
gen-irish-grover-gf-stack-sans-notch: Irish Grover looks fun and organic, its tall lowercase making words seem sturdy and large. But Stack Sans Notch is sans-serif with flat, rod-like strokes, so the soft thick-and-thin lilt above meets a line that never swells.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-stack-sans-text: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy pours its ink at one width under a high mean line. Stack Sans Text is sans-serif with big-bodied lowercase and well-separated curve endings, so it can be sized modestly and still hold its own.
gen-megrim-gf-sulphur-point: Angular, thin and futuristic. Megrim ends every stroke at one measured thickness, and Sulphur Point answers with sans-serif lowercase that is bulky and open, so a slightly smaller size would still feel sturdy beneath it.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-tiktok-sans: Mystery Quest brings a bookish, nostalgic feel, with open jaws on every curve and compact ascenders. TikTok Sans is a modern sans-serif whose tall x-height nearly reaches cap height, and that difference in era is what makes the pairing memorable.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-nunito: Nunito reads soft and approachable, with big round lowercase bowls and terminals that stop well short of the stem. Oswald, confident and tightly knit, earns its keep when it is big and brief.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-quicksand: Tight, strong and confident up top. Oswald packs its rows closely and does its best work as a bold headline, while Quicksand relaxes below it with tall, bulb-like lowercase bowls and one uninterrupted monoline stroke.
